hook: Fill gaps in demanding academic German by checking the form first and the meaning second, a method that rarely lets you down.
intro: This is a cloze on a short academic text, and its gaps sit where formal German is hardest: verbs (meaning, tense, mood), modal verbs, connectors, temporal/causal/modal/local phrases, pronouns. This quiz is that task on a full-length text: eight gaps, four options each. Each gap is solved in two steps: grammar first (what word class and form does the slot demand — a verb in the Präteritum to match its neighbours? a subordinating conjunction because the verb is at the end? an adverb of degree inside a relative clause?), then meaning (which of the survivors fits the argument — concession because the next clause says 'bleibt offen'?). Funktionsverbgefüge are a favourite (legen … nahe, stellen … in Frage, ziehen … in Betracht): learn the light verb. Tense consistency is another: a Präteritum narrative wants Präteritum, with the Plusquamperfekt only for the earlier step. And the Konjunktiv marks reported claims (man vermutet, dass … sei / werde) — watch for it.
tips[0].title: Grammar first: word class and form
tips[0].text: Verb at the end of the clause → the gap before is a subordinator (wenngleich / obwohl), not an adverb. Neighbouring verbs in the Präteritum → the gap verb is Präteritum. A slot between article and noun → adjective. Eliminate by form before you think about sense.
tips[0].check.why: waren stands at the end of its clause, so the gap needs a subordinator; trotzdem and allerdings are adverbs and would need the verb right after them.

tips[1].title: Funktionsverbgefüge and fixed verbs
tips[1].text: nahelegen (suggest): legen … nahe · in Frage stellen · in Betracht ziehen · zur Verfügung stehen · zu dem Schluss kommen · eine Rolle spielen. The gap is usually the light verb; the noun beside it tells you which.
tips[1].trap: 'legen' vs 'liegen': nahelegen (to suggest) is transitive with legen; 'nahe liegen' (to be obvious: es liegt nahe, dass) is a different phrase. The cloze tests exactly this pair.
tips[1].check.why: 'To suggest' is nahelegen, so the light verb is legen; nahe liegen means 'to be obvious' and takes no object.
tips[2].title: Then meaning: the relation to the neighbours
tips[2].text: 'bleibt die Frage offen' after the gap → concession (wenngleich), not condition (sofern) or strengthening (zumal). 'jedoch' in the sentence → the gap is not another contrast word. Read one sentence on each side.
tips[2].check.why: The second clause limits the first, so you need a concession (although); zumal would strengthen and sofern would set a condition.
tips[3].title: Tense: follow the neighbours
tips[3].text: schliefen … erinnerten sich … (both Präteritum); wach geblieben waren (Plusquamperfekt: they had stayed awake before). One tense for the line, one step back for the earlier event. And after "man vermutet, dass" a general mechanism stays in the Präsens.
tips[3].check.why: The line is in the Präteritum, and the earlier step goes one tense back: Plusquamperfekt.
remember[0]: Form first (verb position, tense, word class), then sense.
remember[1]: nahelegen = legen … nahe; the cloze loves light verbs.
exam: A gapped academic text testing verbs, connectors and fixed phrases is a standard reading task in the C1 exam.
